name: sgs/product-search
title: Product Search
description: Accessible combobox search that fetches live product suggestions. Includes a no-JS fallback form that submits to the theme's product-scoped search results page.

sgs._comment_mediaElements: 37-media-no-handroll remediation (2026-09-03). The result-row product thumbnail (`.sgs-product-search__results [role="option"] img`) is built at runtime by view.js (a live REST-fetched results list), not by render.php — there is no server-rendered to attach the marker class to at render time. The scoped custom-property VALUE is still computed server-side by SGS_Media_Element::style() (keyed on the block's existing no-inline scoped-styling uid class, $sgs_style_uid, already present on the wrapper for every display mode), and view.js adds the `sgs-media-el` marker + that same uid class onto each thumbnail it creates, so the shared `.sgs-media-el{object-fit:var(--sgs-media-object-fit,cover)}` atom stylesheet paints it. style.css no longer hardcodes object-fit:cover.

wrapper.label: Search wrapper
wrapper._note: No color, typography or __experimentalBorder support is declared on this block at all. clusters is deliberately scoped to layout (native spacing only) to avoid a zero-resolution declaration (ROLLOUT REQUIREMENT 1).

input.label: Search input
input._note: The search <input class="sgs-product-search__input" role="combobox"> (render.php:326-341). Declared because F6 check #8 (reseed-survival) correctly REFUSED a css_property with no css_element: inputBorderColour resolved to border-color but had css_element=NULL and derived_selector=NULL, so it fell to the ROOT routing domain and would misroute on a clone. A property resolved without an element is not a win — it is a mis-route waiting to happen. ⚠ KNOWN MODELLING LIMIT: --sgs-ps-input-border has TWO consumers — this input's border (style.css:37) AND the listbox border (style.css:87). One attribute paints two nodes; the manifest models attribute->element ownership one-to-one, so it is declared on the input (the primary, named node) and the listbox border rides the same variable. Splitting them would need a second attribute, which is a client-facing control decision, not a mapping one.
